sentences.text: Bagaraatan is a Mongolian theropod dinosaur genus named for its small size, meaning 'small carnivorous animal' in Mongolian.
It was likely a small predator reaching approximately 3 to 4 meters in length.
The species Bagaraatan ostromi was first described by Halszka Osmólska in 1996.
The holotype skeleton — the specimen the species is based on — initially resembled juvenile Tyrannosaurus and Tarbosaurus, suggesting it was one of the smallest known tyrannosaurids.
Later analysis revealed that the original material attributed to Bagaraatan was a mix of bones from two different dinosaurs, including hand bones and a femur from a caenagnathid.
A 2024 study confirmed that the initial material assigned to Bagaraatan was a chimaera of different dinosaur species.
Researchers suggest the holotype material likely belongs to the Tyrannosauridae family or a closely related group.
Scientists caution that the exact evolutionary position of Bagaraatan remains uncertain because juvenile tyrannosaurids often appear more primitive in phylogenetic trees.
Bagaraatan lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
